title: Effects of Creatine Formulations on Exercise and Cognitive Performance
official: Effects of Creatine Monohydrate Versus a Multi-Ingredient Creatine Formulation on Exercise Performance, Cognitive Function, Hydration, and Gastrointestinal Tolerability
summary:
This study will examine whether a multi-ingredient creatine supplement produces different effects on exercise performance, cognitive function, hydration, and gastrointestinal symptoms compared with creatine monohydrate alone.

Approximately 16 healthy, physically active adults aged 18-40 years will participate. Each participant will take creatine monohydrate (5 grams per day) for 18 days and a multi-ingredient supplement containing creatine monohydrate (5 grams), sodium, potassium, magnesium, and taurine for another 18 days. The order of supplementation will be randomly assigned, with a 30-day break between conditions.

Participants will complete laboratory testing before and after each supplementation period. Testing will include bench press exercise to assess muscular endurance, repeated high-intensity cycling tests to assess exercise performance, and a computerized cognitive task to measure attention and reaction time. Researchers will also assess hydration, selected blood markers, perceived exertion, and gastrointestinal symptoms.

The findings may help determine whether adding electrolytes and taurine to creatine provides additional benefits or produces different physiological responses compared with creatine monohydrate alone.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18-40 years.
* Apparently healthy individuals who are physically active and capable of performing vigorous exercise.
* Willing and able to complete repeated maximal-intensity cycling tests, bench press exercise, and cognitive assessments.
* Willing to consume both assigned dietary supplement formulations for 18 days each, separated by a 30-day washout period.
* Willing to refrain from taking additional creatine or electrolyte supplements during the study, including the washout period.
* Able and willing to provide written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, neurological, or musculoskeletal conditions that may contraindicate vigorous exercise or interfere with study outcomes.
* Current injury or physical limitation that would prevent safe completion of the exercise testing procedures.
* Current pregnancy or plans to become pregnant during the study.
* Recent creatine supplementation prior to enrollment.
* Current use of medications or dietary supplements that may interfere with creatine metabolism, hydration status, exercise performance, cognitive function, or participant safety.
* Known allergy, intolerance, or contraindication to any ingredient in the study supplements.
* Unwillingness or inability to comply with supplementation, washout, or laboratory testing requirements.
